title: Word order: who + when + where + do what
summary: Lets you build sentences in the right order: subject, then time, then place, then verb and object.
explanation:
Chinese word order is very regular. The basic order is the same as English, subject + verb + object: 我喝茶. But time and place come BEFORE the verb, not at the end as in English.

So 'I eat at home in the evening' is 我晚上在家吃饭: who (我), when (晚上), where (在家), what (吃饭). The time word may also go first, before the subject: 晚上我在家吃饭. Time always comes before place.

examples.en: In the evening he reads at home.
Today we're eating at a restaurant.
Mum works at the hospital in the mornings.

mistakes.why: Time words go before the verb, not at the end of the sentence.

exercises.en: I'm going to the shop tomorrow.
exercises.why: Who, then when, then the verb and the place: time goes before the verb.

exercises.en: She works at a company in the afternoon.
exercises.why: Time before place, and both before the verb 工作.

why: Time can't go at the end; it comes before the verb.
Time comes before place, not after it.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'We study Chinese at school'?
why: Correct: the place (在学校) goes before the verb.
In Chinese, 在 + place comes before the verb, not at the end.
The object 汉语 comes after the verb, and the subject is near the front.

exercises.en: Dad watches TV at home in the evening.
why: Correct: a time word like 晚上 goes straight before the place and verb, with no 在.
Time words don't take 在: just 晚上.
晚 means 'late'; 'in the evening' is 晚上.

exercises.instruction: Move the time word to the front of the sentence.
why: Correct: a time word can go before the subject.
The time word can go first, but never at the end.
明天 can't sit between the verb and the place.
